content.value_statement: Turning scattered project notes into a formal weekly report takes time and can omit important work. This skill creates a consistent report from execution documents or README version records.
actual_capabilities: Creates a weekly report from execution documents or README version records.
Requests a document path or date range when both are missing.
Uses a fixed title and sections for this week and next week.
Outputs the report body without changing source documents by default.
Writes a report only when the user explicitly requests saving it.
limitations: Requires source documents or a date range to identify relevant work.
Does not modify code, README files, or execution documents by default.
Uses a fixed report structure and does not create alternative layouts.
Cannot verify work that is absent from the provided records.

use_cases.description: Turn project records into a formal update for stakeholders and managers.

best_practices: Provide the source document path and a clear reporting date range.
Review the generated summary before sharing it with colleagues.
Request file saving only after confirming the report content.
anti_patterns: Do not expect the skill to infer work absent from source records.
Do not use it to modify code or project documentation.
Do not request a different report structure when the fixed format is required.

faq.question: What information does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide an execution document path, a date range, or README version records.

faq.question: Does it change my project files?
faq.answer: No. It only writes a report when you explicitly request saving it.

faq.question: What report structure does it use?
faq.answer: It uses a fixed title, reporting period, this week section, and next week section.

faq.question: Can it use README history?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create a report from README version records.

faq.question: Can it create a report without dates?
faq.answer: It asks for a document path or date range when both are missing.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
